A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Attention as a Hypernetwork, with matching main sections and appendices A–D. The text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite formatting changes and expanded appendix content.

before.justification: v3 reports original fuzzy-logic, SRAVEN and C4 experiments, including performance comparisons, ablations and latent-code analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds MoE comparisons, SRAVEN split-sensitivity results and further diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds experimental variants that replace transformer feedforward layers with sparsely gated mixtures of experts, including HYLA + MoE. The core HYLA attention computation, normalization, nonlinearity and pseudocode remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate fuzzy-logic functions, SRAVEN and C4 language modeling. Unseen-term fuzzy-logic testing already appears in v3 Figure A4 and moves into v4 Figure A3C. The new SRAVEN held-out-fraction sweep changes splits within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Table A1 adds Softmax attention + MoE, Linear attention + MoE and HYLA + MoE to both symbolic-task comparisons. All earlier comparator and ablation rows remain.

E3.justification: v4 Figure A5 introduces a SRAVEN evaluation sweep holding out 10%, 30%, 50%, 70% and 90% of rule combinations. The existing default 25% split and Table A3 settings are retained. The newly mentioned mixed-precision training is additional disclosure, without evidence of a changed existing protocol.

E4.justification: The appendix substantially broadens the analysis: MoE ablations test another form of modular computation; Figure A5 tests SRAVEN split sensitivity; Figures A3D and A4 add training-loss diagnostics. Figure A8 adds individual-head and rule-average attention analyses and extends cosine-similarity comparisons to softmax and linear attention. Earlier t-SNE and unseen-term analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table A1 reports standard errors over three seeds in both versions, including the added MoE rows in v4. Table A2 retains its 4096-instance Monte Carlo estimate and standard errors. No new uncertainty-estimation practice or increased run count is stated.

E6.justification: Figure 5C revises HYLA's one-head SRAVEN OOD accuracy from approximately 0 to 0.41, materially changing the severity of this mechanistic-ablation result without a stated protocol revision. Table A1 adds SRAVEN scores of 57.68, 64.34 and 66.94 for Softmax attention + MoE, Linear attention + MoE and HYLA + MoE, respectively, while retaining all earlier rows. New split-sensitivity, training-loss and attention-code results further expand the evidence.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds an explicit mathematical definition of the Top_k-gated MoE computation. The main attention-to-hypernetwork derivation, HYLA equations and SRAVEN counting argument are retained. Matrix-orientation and symbol changes otherwise standardize notation; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions and discussion retain the same central claims: attention admits a hypernetwork interpretation, latent codes reflect reusable operations, scaling supports compositional generalization, HYLA improves symbolic-task generalization, and SRAVEN enables controlled evaluation.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 replaces the assertion that visual abstraction is usually not Raven's main difficulty with a more cautious account of difficulty remaining after symbolic abstraction. Section 4.4 expands the single-head rescaling explanation. Appendix A.1 interprets MoE effects as comparable to ordinary capacity increases and removes the earlier speculative explanation for the softmax ablation. The stated pretrained-model limitation remains.

D1.justification: v4 newly discloses mixed-precision language-model training and explicitly clarifies that RMS normalization has no learnable scale. It describes MoE routing, although numerical expert and routing counts are unspecified. Existing hyperparameter tables, hardware, runtime estimates, software and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Zhang and Sennrich (2019) and Glorot and Bengio (2010) for normalization and initialization, and develops the relationship to already-cited MoE work. Section 4.1 drops v3's specific assertion that finding correspondences had not been explicitly considered in previous Raven benchmarks. The broader related-work positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v4 copyedits the prose, locally rewrites the introduction and SRAVEN task explanation, replaces much main-text 'query token' terminology with 'response token', and standardizes SRAVEN symbols. Citations switch to author–year format. The main section and appendix organization remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with clearer colored feature correspondences, Table A1 gains a separate MoE block, and the appendix consolidates existing fuzzy-logic plots into Figure A3 while adding Figures A4, A5 and A8. Figure 5C changes its axis range and markers. Together with the ICLR template and redistributed figures, these substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The MoE comparisons, SRAVEN split-sensitivity test and additional diagnostics make the existing explanation easier to assess, while the revised Figure 3 clarifies the benchmark. These provide a limited overall improvement. The gain is constrained by unspecified MoE routing settings and the unexplained single-head result revision in Figure 5C; the central findings and stated limitations remain largely unchanged.
